item.title: Flying Fijians to drop to 10th in World Rugby rankings after Japan loss
item.description: The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will drop from ninth to 10th in the World Rugby rankings after losing 20-15 to Japan in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final. Fiji entered the tournament with high expectations, hoping to finish their campaign by lifting the Pacific Nations Cup trophy.
item.content:encoded:
The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will drop from ninth to 10th in the World Rugby rankings after losing 20-15 to Japan in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final.

Fiji entered the tournament with high expectations, hoping to finish their campaign by lifting the Pacific Nations Cup trophy.

Instead, Japan produced a determined performance in the final, leaving the Fijian side facing not only the disappointment of missing out on the title but also a drop in the World Rugby rankings.

The defeat will see Fiji slip to 10th in the rankings, while Japan’s victory will give the Brave Blossoms a significant boost.

item.title: Fiji Rakavi strengthens Governance and Charts Course for 2027
item.description: The review covered the Vodafone Vanua and Royal Tea Ranadi provincial competitions, including Northern Bulls, Ovalau, Namosi, Serua and Nasinu, as well as the Vodafone Deans, Weet-Bix Raluve and Vodafone Juniors competitions. FRU says the session brought together key stakeholders to assess the 2026 season, identify key strengths and challenges, capture lessons learned, and set priorities for impro
item.content:encoded:
The review covered the Vodafone Vanua and Royal Tea Ranadi provincial competitions, including Northern Bulls, Ovalau, Namosi, Serua and Nasinu, as well as the Vodafone Deans, Weet-Bix Raluve and Vodafone Juniors competitions.

FRU says the session brought together key stakeholders to assess the 2026 season, identify key strengths and challenges, capture lessons learned, and set priorities for improving the delivery of competitions in 2027.

They say the session also examined financial acquittals from the Schools Rugby, Vanua and Ranadi treasurers, reinforcing Fiji Rakavi’s commitment to sound financial management, transparency and accountability across the game.

The review process provides an important opportunity to assess how competitions were delivered, identify operational and administrative gaps, capture stakeholder feedback, and apply lessons from the 2026 season to strengthen planning and delivery for 2027.

The next review will be held in the Northern Division next week, followed by the Western Division the following week.

FRU says the Skipper Cup and Marama Championship will be reviewed separately at the conclusion of their respective competitions.

They say as Fiji Rakavi looks towards 2027, the focus remains on strengthening governance, improving competition delivery, and building a sustainable rugby pathway from grassroots and schools through to provincial and national representation.

item.title: Fiji Kulas hunt for first win against Vanuatu tonight
item.description: The Fiji Kulas will be hunting for their first win of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 when they take on Vanuatu at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva tonight. The Kulas will be looking to bounce back after going down 4-0 to Papua New Guinea in their opening match.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Kulas will be hunting for their first win of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 when they take on Vanuatu at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva tonight.

The Kulas will be looking to bounce back after going down 4-0 to Papua New Guinea in their opening match.

Vanuatu, meanwhile, started their campaign with a 1-all draw against the Solomon Islands.

The women’s competition continues at 4pm today with New Caledonia taking on Papua New Guinea before Fiji faces Vanuatu at 7pm.

Meanwhile, in the men’s competition, Papua New Guinea beat Vanuatu 2-1 on Friday, while the Bula Boys were held to a thrilling 3-all draw by the Solomon Islands.

The men’s competition continues tomorrow with New Caledonia taking on the Solomon Islands at 4pm, before the Bula Boys face Vanuatu at 7pm.

item.title: Nadroga end Nadi’s unbeaten run in Skipper Cup thriller
item.description: The highly anticipated Western derby lived up to expectations as the two sides battled through an intense and physical 80 minutes. Nadroga opened the scoring in the 18th minute after Nadi lost possession while on attack.
item.content:encoded:
The highly anticipated Western derby lived up to expectations as the two sides battled through an intense and physical 80 minutes.

Nadroga opened the scoring in the 18th minute after Nadi lost possession while on attack.

The Stallions quickly turned defence into attack, with centre Kavekini Boselawa finishing off the counter-attack to give the visitors an early 5–0 lead.

Nadi responded through flanker Peni Vukivuki, bringing the home side back into the contest.

Nadroga, however, regained the advantage when full-back Sefanaia Tokaduadua crossed the try line, giving the visitors a 10–7 lead at half-time.

Tight-head prop Josh Uluibau powered his way over the line in the 62nd minute, sending the home crowd into celebration as Nadi moved ahead 14–10.

Both sides then exchanged penalties as the pressure continued to build.

With the match entering its final stages, Nadroga were dealt another setback when they were reduced to 14 men after receiving a red card.

Their persistence was eventually rewarded when replacement hooker Apenisa Lanivia crashed over the try line to score the winning try.

The late effort secured a dramatic 20–17 victory for Nadroga and brought Nadi’s unbeaten run to an end.

In other results Suva edged Malolo 31-27, Lautoka beat Tailevu 27-22, Naitasiri defeated Ba 33-28, Navosa egded Rewa 39-38 while Taveuni drew with Kadavu 12 all.
